title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-26
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 5♣. It seems natural to play the ♠K or ♠Q from dummy, but there is great risk in that play. East will win the ♠A and switch to hearts. If West has the ♥K, the defense will be able to take 3 tricks (the ♣A must be knocked out before diamonds are played).

South can improve his chances by ducking in dummy at trick 1. East cannot afford to play the ♠A (that would set up 2 quick discards for South's hearts). East must duck leaving West on lead. West cannot profitably attack hearts from his side of the table. West does best to switch to a trump. If East wins the ♣A and switches to a heart, South wins the ♥A.

After drawing trump, South can set up a spade winner in dummy by taking a ruffing finesse against East's ♠A. North will have 2 winners (a spade trick and the long diamond) to take care of South's heart losers.
